text: When you design a REST API, you should follow some simple best practices. First, give your endpoints clear names that describe the resource, such as /users or /orders. Use the correct HTTP methods and return proper status codes, for example 200 for success and 404 when something is not found. Good documentation is also essential, because it helps other developers understand how to use your API. Finally, always add versioning, such as /v1/users, so you can make changes later without breaking existing applications. By following these rules, you can build APIs that are reliable and easy to work with.
